query: For single-phase ZrB2 ceramic, which requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C and may lack the strength and structural integrity needed for service, what single intervention could lower the required preparation temperature and reduce the holes and eventual component failure caused by prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath? State one hypothesis identifying the intervention and its mechanism, predict its performance compared with conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2, define the relevant preparation and service boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and describe a controlled preparation, integrity, and long-duration exposure experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.material_initial_state: A mixed powder consisting of ZrB2 ceramic powder (>99.8% purity, 1–5 μm) and 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder prepared from equimolar Al, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cr powders by ball milling; the powders were ethanol-milled and vacuum-dried before sintering.
generation.intervention: ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets were consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 1300, 1400, 1500, or 1600 °C to determine the sintering temperature giving the best mechanical properties and resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion and wear.
generation.conditions: SPS was performed under vacuum at 50 MPa, approximately 200 °C/min, with a 5 min hold. Corrosion specimens were immersed in molten Al at 700 °C for 4, 8, or 12 days. Ball-on-disc wear tests used a Si3N4 ball at room temperature, 10 N load, 500 r/min, and 30 min.
generation.structural_mediator: Increasing Mo produced Mo-induced FCC lattice distortion and increasing amounts of a hard, Mo-rich tetragonal σ phase, while Ag, Ni/MoS2, and Cr2O3 remained distributed mainly along matrix-powder boundaries. During sliding, Ni/MoS2-Ag-rich lubricating films operated at low-to-medium temperature, whereas oxide/molybdate tribofilms formed at high temperature; Mo1 developed a particularly continuous, dense glaze at 800 °C containing NiO and Ag2MoO4, Ag2Mo4O13, and Ag2Mo2O7.
generation.mechanism: Dissolved Mo impedes dislocation motion through solid-solution strengthening, and the hard σ phase suppresses plastic deformation and scratching through second-phase strengthening. At lower temperatures, layered MoS2 supplies a low-shear film and soft Ag reduces adhesion, although thermal softening and rough wear tracks at 200–400 °C hinder formation of a continuous lubricant layer. At 600–800 °C, oxidation and tribochemical reactions generate layered silver molybdates and other oxides; compaction of these products into a glaze separates the matrix from the counterface and reduces interfacial shear and material removal.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C, the 1500 °C material should exhibit the greatest density, hardness, and fracture toughness, the lowest molten-Al corrosion rate and wear volume, and more stable friction behavior; its fracture toughness should also exceed that of pure ZrB2.
generation.baseline: ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, and 1600 °C served as the principal processing baselines; pure ZrB2 ceramics (reported fracture toughness 4.5 MPa·m^1/2) were used as a toughness reference.
generation.boundary: The optimum was observed for the tested 30%-binder ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr composition sintered at 1500 °C under the stated SPS schedule. Performance declined at 1600 °C because of binder overflow. Corrosion conclusions apply to molten Al at 700 °C for up to 12 days, and wear conclusions apply to the specified room-temperature ball-on-disc test.

falsification_experiment.design: SEM/EDS and XRD characterized phases, pores, interfaces, and corrosion layers; Archimedes relative density, Vickers hardness/indentation fracture toughness, thickness-loss corrosion rate after molten-Al exposure, wear volume, and friction coefficient distinguished the four sintering conditions.
measurements: SEM/EDS and XRD characterized phases, pores, interfaces, and corrosion layers; Archimedes relative density, Vickers hardness/indentation fracture toughness, thickness-loss corrosion rate after molten-Al exposure, wear volume, and friction coefficient distinguished the four sintering conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
